finding.claim: Unvalidated profile icon URL is stored by update() and fetched server-side by the nightly sync() job, letting an authenticated user make the server issue GET requests to arbitrary http/https destinations, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints (blind: response body is discarded).
finding.source: PUT /profile request parameter `icon` -> update(String webhook, String icon) at src/Profile.java:11, stored at line 16 (this.iconUrl = icon) with no validation
finding.sink: HttpClient.send(HttpRequest.newBuilder().uri(URI.create(iconUrl)).GET().build(), ofByteArray()) at src/Profile.java:23-24, executed from sync() in the nightly job

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives attacker-controlled icon from PUT /profile
regex guard applies only to `webhook`; `icon` is not checked
this.iconUrl = icon stores the raw attacker string
sync(HttpClient c) runs as a nightly job with the server's network position and credentials
URI.create(iconUrl) parses the stored string with no host, IP, port, or scheme check
c.send issues GET to the attacker-chosen URL; the response is read into a byte array and not returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: (1) webhook regex at line 12 does not cover icon, so no validation on the icon path; (2) sync() performs no allowlist of hosts, no private/link-local/loopback IP blocking, and no DNS pinning; (3) java.net.http.HttpRequest only accepts http/https schemes, which blocks file:, gopher:, and similar schemes but not internal http targets such as 169.254.169.254 or localhost; (4) redirect policy is set on the HttpClient `c` passed in, which is not visible here, so if it follows redirects an allowed host could redirect to an internal one; (5) the path into update() is not visible here, so any auth or authorization check on PUT /profile is unknown and may limit who can reach this sink.

verdict.guard_found: none. No validation of `icon` exists on the path: src/Profile.java:12 regex covers only `webhook`, and src/Profile.java:16 stores `icon` unchecked. sync() at src/Profile.java:20-24 has no host, IP, or scheme allowlist.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (src/Profile.java:11, 12, 16, 20, 23) and no closing guard exists on the icon path, but the source is not established: the only evidence of a remote PUT /profile route is the comment at src/Profile.java:10, and the directory contains no handler, so whether an authenticated low-privilege user can reach update() with an attacker-chosen `icon` cannot be decided from the code available. The HttpClient's redirect and network configuration, which the candidate itself flags as unknown, is also not visible.
